mainTopic: Who may make a wife or widow swear when she collects her כתובה, and how the husband's waiver wording affects it
overview: The גמרא asks which oath a husband meant when he wrote that he would not make his wife swear. רב יהודה says it is the oath about managing his property during his life. רבה בר אבוה says it is the oath of a woman who admits she took part of her כתובה. When רב מרדכי asks how a bride could know in advance that she would become a manager, רב אשי answers that רב יהודה's words really explain a different line of the משנה. That line says the heirs cannot make a widow swear about 'the past'. רב יהודה adds that they can make her swear about the time between death and burial, and רב מתנא disagrees. Next comes a debate about the husband's exact wording: 'not an oath', 'clear of oath', 'my property', 'these properties'. The הלכה follows אבא שאול בן אימא מרים: any wording frees her, but she must still swear when collecting from orphans. A new משנה then lists five cases where a woman collects her כתובה only with an oath, and explains each one.

steps.title: The oath was about managing his property during his life
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רב יהודה's answer. The husband excused his wife from an oath about her time as manager of his property while he was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to a woman who was made manager of his property while her husband was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב יהודה's answer to the question of which oath the husband had in mind when he wrote that he would not make her swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband often put his wife in charge of his property. A manager normally has to swear that she did not take anything for herself. According to רב יהודה, this is the oath the husband excused her from.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman put in charge of managing property

phrases.english: About a woman who became a manager during her husband's lifetime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's answer to the question raised before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's written exemption covers the oath of a wife who managed his property while he was alive.

steps.title: Another view: the oath of a woman who took part of her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, says the exemption refers to the oath of a woman who admits she already received part of her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it refers to a woman who has reduced her כתובה by taking part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question about which oath the husband had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who admits she already took part of her כתובה must swear that she took no more than she says. According to this view, that is the oath the husband excused her from.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who reduces her כתובה by admitting she already received part of it

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
About a woman who reduces her marriage contract.
phrases.notes: She admits she already received part of it, so she would normally have to swear she got no more than that.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רב יהודה answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption covers the oath of a woman who admits she partly collected her כתובה.

steps.title: How would a bride know to ask about managing property?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי asks רב אשי a question. Taking part of a כתובה is something a bride can plan for. But how would she know in advance that she would become a manager?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי went and told this teaching to רב אשי. He said: It makes sense according to the one who says the oath is about a woman who reduces her כתובה. She thinks: 'Maybe I will need money and take some from my כתובה.' So she says to him: 'Write for me that you will not make me swear.' But according to the one who says it is about a woman who became manager during her husband's lifetime: did she know he would make her a manager, so that she would say to him, 'Write for me that you will not make me swear'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי challenges רב יהודה's view. A bride would not know ahead of time to ask for an exemption from an oath about managing property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is something the woman asks for when they marry. Needing money from her כתובה is easy to imagine ahead of time. Being made manager depends on a later choice by her husband, so why would she think to ask about it?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (according to one view)
Since it comes to her mind

phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai went,
and said this teaching before Rav Ashi:
It makes sense according to the one who says
it is about a woman who reduces her marriage contract,
since it comes to her mind:
Perhaps I will need money,
and I will take it from my marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה לֵיהּ: כְּתוֹב לִי דְּלָא מַשְׁבְּעַתְּ לִי.
phrases.english: so she says to him: Write for me that you will not make me swear.
But according to the one who says
it is about a woman who became a manager during her husband's lifetime,
did she know
that he would set her up as a manager,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרָה לֵיהּ: ״כְּתוֹב לִי דְּלָא מַשְׁבְּעַתְּ לִי״?
phrases.english: so that she would say to him: 'Write for me that you will not make me swear'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַל הַפּוֹגֶמֶת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two views and challenges the first one (רב יהודה).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that the exemption covers an oath about managing property during the husband's life.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exemption comes from the woman's request at the start of the marriage. She cannot foresee being made manager, but she can foresee taking money from her כתובה.

steps.title: רב אשי: we teach it on a different line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says his yeshiva attaches רב יהודה's statement to a later line of the משנה. That line is about a widow, and about what the heirs may make her swear about.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You teach it on that line; we teach it on this line: If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house, or went back to her father-in-law's house and did not become a manager, the heirs do not make her swear. If she did become a manager, the heirs make her swear about the future, but they do not make her swear about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by saying it starts from the wrong place. רב יהודה was not explaining the line about the husband's written exemption. He was explaining a different line of the משנה, which רב אשי now quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יהודה was not explaining what the bride asked for, the question 'how did she know?' falls away. The line רב אשי quotes says the heirs can make a manager-widow swear about the future but not about the past. That sets up the next question: what does 'the past' mean?

keyTerms.meaning: About the future (after the husband's death)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying רב יהודה was wrong. He is saying רב יהודה's words were said about a different line of the משנה, so the question does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: Moving which line of the משנה a statement explains is a common way the גמרא answers a question without rejecting the אמורא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתּוּן, אַהָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: You teach it on that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means the earlier line about the husband writing that he won't make her swear.

phrases.english: we teach it on this:
If she went from her husband's grave to her father's house,
or she returned to her father-in-law's house
and did not become a manager,
the heirs do not make her swear.
And if she became a manager,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹרְשִׁין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,
phrases.english: the heirs make her swear about the future,
phrases.notes: The future means whatever she does with the property after her husband's death.

phrases.english: but they do not make her swear about the past.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן אַהָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ אֲנַן אַהָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מרדכי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attaches רב יהודה's statement to a different line of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה was explaining which oath the bride asked to be excused from.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה was explaining the line about 'the past' in the case of a widow and the heirs, so the bride's foresight does not matter.

steps.title: What does 'the past' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: Still speaking for his yeshiva, רב אשי quotes the question: what oath about the past would the heirs even want from her?
steps.simpleTranslation: The past — what does it have to do with this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes the question his yeshiva asked about the line he just brought. This sets up the answer of רב יהודה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the heirs cannot make her swear about the past. The question is what past oath would ever come up, so that the משנה needs to rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its purpose / what does it have to do with this?

phrases.english: The past — what does it have to do with this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last line of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What oath about the past the משנה is ruling out.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the past means managing during the husband's life
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of רב, answers that 'the past' means her time as manager while her husband was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It refers to a woman who became a manager during the husband's lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: This is where רב יהודה's statement belongs according to רב אשי. It explains which past oath the heirs cannot demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same words of רב יהודה as before, but now they answer 'what is the past?' instead of 'what did the bride ask for?'. So רב מרדכי's question about the bride's foresight no longer applies. The sentence continues in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רב יהודה's words explain the 'past' that the heirs cannot make the widow swear about. They do not explain what the bride asked her husband to write.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is about a woman who became a manager during the husband's lifetime,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The past' means her time as manager while her husband was alive.

steps.title: Except the days between death and burial
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's answer continues: the heirs cannot make her swear about her time as manager during her husband's life, but they can make her swear about what happened between his death and his burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the time between his death and his burial, we do make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב יהודה's answer from the last step by adding a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's waiver only covered the time when he was alive and she managed his property. Between his death and burial she was handling money that now belonged to the heirs. So, says רב יהודה, the heirs may make her swear about that short window.

keyTerms.meaning: Between death and burial: the short time after the husband dies and before he is buried.

phrases.english: But between death and burial,
we do make her swear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בֵּין מִיתָה לִקְבוּרָה מַשְׁבְּעִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's definition of 'the past' by carving out the time between death and burial.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heirs can make her swear about her conduct between her husband's death and his burial.

steps.title: No oath even between death and burial
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא disagrees and says the heirs cannot make her swear even about the time between death and burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מתנא said: even about the time between death and burial, we do not make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא argues with the limit רב יהודה just set. In the next step he gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, the days between death and burial are open to an oath. For רב מתנא, even that window is protected, so the widow does not swear about it at all.

phrases.english: And רב מתנא said:
Even between death and burial,
we do not make her swear,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב מַתְנָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ בֵּין מִיתָה לִקְבוּרָה לָא מַשְׁבְּעִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the exception given in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No oath is given to the widow, even for the time between death and burial.

steps.title: The ruling of נהרדעא about urgent sales
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא supports his view with a teaching of the people of נהרדעא: for head tax, food, and burial, the court sells the orphans' property without the usual public announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the people of נהרדעא say: to pay head tax, to buy food, and for burial, we sell property without an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא brings a proof for his view from a known ruling about urgent needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a court announces a sale of orphans' property so it gets a fair price. For urgent needs like a burial, the court skips this and accepts a possible loss. In the same way, during the rush before a burial the widow is not expected to keep exact accounts, so she does not have to swear about that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of נהרדעא, a city in Babylonia.
Head tax, a tax charged per person.
A public announcement before the court sells property.

phrases.english: For the people of נהרדעא say:
For head tax, for food, and for burial,
we sell without an announcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב מתנא's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב מתנא's ruling that no oath is given for the time between death and burial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of נהרדעא that in urgent times, such as before a burial, the court does not insist on the usual careful steps.

steps.title: רבה's version of רבי חייא on the waiver wording
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רבי חייא: if the husband wrote 'not a vow and not an oath,' only he cannot make her swear, but his heirs can. If he wrote 'clear of vow, clear of oath,' neither he nor the heirs can, because it means 'you are clear of the oath.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי חייא: 'Not a vow and not an oath' means he cannot make her swear, but the heirs can. 'Clear of vow, clear of oath' means neither he nor the heirs can make her swear. This is what he is telling her: you are free from the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts: how the exact words a husband writes to free his wife from oaths decide who can still make her swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not a vow, not an oath' is read as a personal promise from the husband, so it does not bind his heirs. 'Clear of vow, clear of oath' is read as a full release that frees her completely, so even the heirs cannot make her swear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Not a vow and not an oath': one way a husband words the release.
'Clear of vow, clear of oath': another way of wording it.

phrases.english: רבה said that רבי חייא said:
If he wrote 'Not a vow and not an oath,'
he cannot make her swear,
but the heirs can make her swear.
If he wrote 'Clear of vow, clear of oath,'
both he and the heirs
cannot make her swear.
This is what he is saying to her:
You are clear of the oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about how the husband words his release.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Not a vow, not an oath' frees her only from the husband. 'Clear of vow, clear of oath' frees her from the heirs as well.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes רבי חייא the same way for 'not a vow, not an oath.' But for 'clear of vow, clear of oath,' he says both the husband and the heirs can make her swear, because it means 'clear yourself through an oath.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רבי חייא: 'Not a vow and not an oath' means he cannot make her swear, but the heirs can. 'Clear of vow, clear of oath' means both he and the heirs can make her swear. This is what he is telling her: clear yourself by taking an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי חייא's teaching, which flips the meaning of the second wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree about 'not a vow, not an oath.' They argue about the word נקי. רבה reads it as 'you are free,' but רב יוסף reads it as 'make yourself clean,' which means proving your honesty by swearing. So in רב יוסף's version, this wording frees her from nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word נקי means opposite things in the two versions: 'you are already free of the oath' for רבה, and 'free yourself by taking the oath' for רב יוסף.

phrases.english: And רב יוסף said that רבי חייא said:
If he wrote 'Not a vow and not an oath,'
he cannot make her swear,
but the heirs can make her swear.
If he wrote 'Clear of vow, clear of oath,'
both he and the heirs
can make her swear.
This is what he is saying to her:
Clear yourself by means of an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי חייא that reverses the ruling on 'clear of vow, clear of oath.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Clear of vow, clear of oath' does not free her at all. Both the husband and the heirs can make her swear.

steps.title: רבי זכאי: 'my property' versus 'these properties'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי sends a ruling to מר עוקבא: it makes no difference whether the husband said 'not' or 'clear.' What matters is whether he wrote 'in my property,' which frees her only from him, or 'from these properties,' which frees her from the heirs too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זכאי sent to מר עוקבא: whether he wrote 'not an oath' or 'clear of oath,' 'not a vow' or 'clear of vow,' if he wrote 'in my property,' he cannot make her swear but the heirs can. If he wrote 'from these properties,' neither he nor his heirs can make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זכאי gives a different rule: the words 'not' and 'clear' do not matter. The deciding words are about the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In my property' ties the release to the husband as owner, so once the property passes to the heirs they may make her swear. 'From these properties' ties the release to the property itself, so it stays in force even after the heirs inherit.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the release wording. רבה: 'clear' frees her from the heirs as well. רב יוסף: 'clear' means she must swear. רבי זכאי: only 'from these properties' frees her from the heirs.

phrases.english: רבי זכאי sent to מר עוקבא:
Whether 'not an oath' or 'clear of oath,'
whether 'not a vow' or 'clear of vow':
if he wrote 'in my property,'
he cannot make her swear,
but the heirs can make her swear.
If he wrote 'from these properties,'
both he and his heirs
cannot make her swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the deciding factor away from 'not' versus 'clear' and onto 'my property' versus 'these properties.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever word he used for the oath, 'in my property' frees her only from the husband, while 'from these properties' frees her from the heirs too.

steps.title: Any wording frees her, but orphans still need an oath
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל in the name of אבא שאול בן אימא מרים: whatever wording the husband used, neither he nor his heirs can make her swear. But because of the rule about collecting from orphans, she must swear anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל, quoting אבא שאול בן אימא מרים: Whether the husband wrote 'not an oath' or 'clear of an oath,' 'not a vow' or 'clear of a vow,' 'from my property' or 'from these properties,' neither he nor his heirs can make her swear. But what can I do? The חכמים said that anyone who collects from orphans' property collects only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is quoted that ignores all the wording differences from the earlier steps. By the husband's release alone, nobody can make her swear, but she still swears when collecting from orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה, רב יוסף and רבי זכאי all made the outcome depend on the exact words. אבא שאול says the words don't matter at all, since every version fully releases her. The oath comes back only through a separate general rule: anyone collecting from orphans must swear, whatever the husband wrote.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose view is quoted here
What can I do? (I have no choice)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he is contradicting himself. The husband's wording really does free her. The oath comes from a different rule that protects orphans, not from anything the husband wrote.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן אִימָּא מִרְיָם:
phrases.english: in the name of Abba Shaul ben Imma Miriam:
Whether he wrote 'not an oath' or 'clear of an oath,'
whether 'not a vow' or 'clear of a vow,'
whether 'from my property' or 'from these properties':
neither he nor his heirs
can make her swear.
But what can I do,
since the Sages said:
One who comes to collect from orphans' property
may collect only with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן אִימָּא מִרְיָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a view that rejects the wording distinctions made by רבה, רב יוסף and רבי זכאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any form of release frees her from both the husband and the heirs, but collecting from orphans always requires an oath.

steps.title: The same teaching quoted as a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some say this teaching is not a quote passed down by רב נחמן but a ברייתא, with אבא שאול בן אימא מרים saying the same thing directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it as a ברייתא: אבא שאול בן אימא מרים said: Whether 'not an oath' or 'clear of an oath,' 'not a vow' or 'clear of a vow,' 'in my property' or 'from these properties,' neither he nor his heirs can make her swear. But what can I do, since the חכמים said that one who collects from orphans' property collects only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where the same teaching comes from. The content is identical. Only the source changes: here it is a ברייתא instead of an אמורא's quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב נחמן and שמואל pass the teaching along. In this version it is a ברייתא, a teaching from the period of the תנאים, quoted directly. The ruling itself does not change.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say it (in a different way)
A ברייתא: a teaching from the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: And some say it as a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל בֶּן אִימָּא מִרְיָם אָמַר:
phrases.english: Abba Shaul ben Imma Miriam said:
Whether 'not an oath' or 'clear of an oath,'
whether 'not a vow' or 'clear of a vow,'
whether 'from my property' or 'from these properties':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הוּא וּבֵין יוֹרְשָׁיו אֵין מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: neither he nor his heirs can make her swear,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: but what can I do, since the Sages said:
One who comes to collect from orphans' property
may collect only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats step 13's teaching, but places its source in a ברייתא instead of an אמורא's quote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same as step 13, now coming from a ברייתא.

steps.title: The הלכה follows בן אימא מרים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows בן אימא מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows בן אימא מרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion of the husband's wording with a final ruling: we follow אבא שאול בן אימא מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the long disagreement in the earlier steps. The exact words of the release don't matter, so neither the husband nor his heirs can make her swear because of the release. She still swears when collecting from orphans, because of the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Short name for אבא שאול בן אימא מרים

steps.whatToRemember: הלכה: every form of release is the same and frees her from both the husband and the heirs. Only the orphans' rule brings back the oath when she collects from orphans.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for any כתובה that includes a release from oaths.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows ben Imma Miriam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on the view in steps 13 and 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אבא שאול בן אימא מרים: the wording of the release makes no difference.

steps.title: New משנה: cases where she collects only with an oath
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases where a woman can collect her כתובה only after swearing: she admits partial payment, one witness says it was paid, she collects from orphans or from sold property, or she collects when the husband is not present.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who reduces her כתובה collects only with an oath. If one witness says it was paid, she collects only with an oath. From orphans' property, from property that has been sold to others, or when he is not present, she collects only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists situations where a woman must swear before collecting her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case gives a reason to doubt her claim, or protects someone who can't defend himself. She herself admits part was paid. A single witness says it was paid. The orphans, the buyers of the property, or the absent husband can't argue against her. In every one of these cases the oath protects the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who reduces her כתובה by admitting part was paid
Property tied to the debt that was sold to someone else

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who reduces her ketubah
may collect only with an oath.
If one witness testifies that it is paid,
she may collect only with an oath.
From orphans' property, or from property sold to others,
or not in his presence,
phrases.notes: 'His' means the husband's: she is collecting while he isn't there.

phrases.english: she may collect only with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹגֶמֶת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ — לֹא תִּפָּרַע אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The case of collecting from orphans connects to the rule quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial admission, one witness, orphans' property, sold property, or the husband's absence each require an oath before she collects.

steps.title: What reducing her כתובה looks like
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the first case: her כתובה was a thousand זוז, the husband says she got it all, and she says she got only a מנה. She collects the rest only with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does a woman reduce her כתובה? Her כתובה was a thousand זוז. He told her, 'You already received your כתובה,' and she says, 'I received only a מנה.' She collects only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to its first case and explains it with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By admitting she already got part of the money, she weakens her own document. So she must swear before collecting the rest. The case is like someone who admits part of a claim and denies the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנה, equal to one hundred זוז

phrases.english: A woman who reduces her ketubah, how so?
If her ketubah was a thousand zuz,
and he said to her: You received your ketubah,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת: לֹא הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי אֶלָּא מָנֶה —
phrases.english: and she says: I received only a maneh,
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred זוז, so she admits receiving a tenth of it.

phrases.english: she may collect only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains with an example the first case listed in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she admits partial payment against his claim of full payment, she collects the rest only with an oath.

steps.title: One witness says the כתובה was already paid
steps.stepSummary: The husband says she was paid in full, she denies it, and one עד backs the husband. She can still collect, but only after a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'one witness says it was paid'? Her כתובה was a thousand זוז. The husband said: 'You already got your כתובה.' She says: 'I did not get it.' And one witness testifies that it was paid. She can collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the second case from its list: a single witness supports the husband's claim that the כתובה was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness is not enough to cancel her כתובה completely, so she can still collect. But his testimony is strong enough to make her swear before she collects. So the witness does not block her. He only adds the requirement of a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness, not the full pair of two
How so? What is the case? The משנה uses it to explain each item on its list

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the witness ends her claim. Even though the witness backs the husband, she still collects. The witness only forces her to swear first.

phrases.aramaic: עֵד אֶחָד מְעִידָהּ שֶׁהִיא פְּרוּעָה, כֵּיצַד?
phrases.english: One witness testifies that it is paid, how so?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the כתובה. This is the second case from the list in Step 16.

phrases.english: Her כתובה was a thousand zuz,
and he said to her: You received your כתובה,
and she says: I did not receive it,
and one witness testifies that it is paid
she may collect only with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אֶחָד מְעִידָהּ שֶׁהִיא פְּרוּעָה, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case-by-case explanation of the list in Step 16, after Step 17 explained the first case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness says the כתובה was paid and she denies it, she collects only with a שבועה.

steps.title: Collecting from property the husband sold
steps.stepSummary: If the husband sold his property to buyers and she collects her כתובה from those buyers, she needs a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of collecting from liened property? He sold his property to others, and she collects from the buyers. She can collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the third case: she collects her כתובה from land the husband sold to other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her כתובה gives her a claim on his land. That claim stays on the land even after he sells it, so she can take it from the buyers. But because she is taking from people who paid for the land, she must first swear that she was not already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Property tied to a debt. Here, land the husband sold that her כתובה still has a claim on

phrases.english: From liened property, how so?
He sold his property to others
and she collects from the buyers
she may collect only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case on the משנה's list, explained in the same 'כיצד' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who collects her כתובה from buyers of her husband's land collects only with a שבועה.

steps.title: Collecting from the orphans
steps.stepSummary: If the husband died and left his property to his heirs, she collects from them only with a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of collecting from orphans' property? He died and left his property to orphans, and she collects from the orphans. She can collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the fourth case: after the husband's death she collects her כתובה from his heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heirs cannot know whether their father already paid her, so the court protects them. This is the same rule mentioned in Step 13: whoever collects from orphans must swear first.

phrases.english: From the property of orphans, how so?
He died and left his property to orphans,
and she collects from the orphans
she may collect only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case on the משנה's list. It connects to the orphans rule mentioned in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow collecting her כתובה from her husband's heirs collects only with a שבועה.

steps.title: Collecting while the husband is away
steps.stepSummary: If the husband went overseas and she collects her כתובה while he is not there, she needs a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'not in his presence'? He went away overseas, and she collects while he is not there. She can collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the last case on its list: she collects her כתובה while the husband is far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the husband is not there to say 'I already paid you,' the court makes her swear to protect him. With this, the משנה has explained every case from its list in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in his presence, while he is absent
A country overseas, a faraway land

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's five cases where a woman collects her כתובה only with a שבועה: (1) she admits she got part, (2) one witness says it was paid, (3) she collects from buyers of his land, (4) she collects from orphans, (5) she collects while he is away.

phrases.english: And not in his presence, how so?
He went away to a country overseas,
and she collects not in his presence
she collects only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last case on the משנה's list. It completes the explanation of all the cases from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who collects her כתובה while her husband is away collects only with a שבועה.
